sub_answers.text: Waves of Kurdish tribes and families arrived into Syria from Turkey beginning in the 1920s, and Kurdish migration to Jazira accelerated after WWI with road networks and the railway extension to Nusaybin. [d3821855s8p0] In the 1920s, failed Kurdish rebellions in Kemalist Turkey led to large refugee waves, with an estimated 20,000–25,000 Kurds settling in Jazira during the 1920s and villages numbering 700–800 by 1939. [d3821855s8p0] In Damascus, Kurds are linked to the neighborhood Rukn al-Din, formerly known as Hayy al Akrad (Kurdish Quarter), and Aleppo has Kurdish neighborhoods including al Ashrafiya and Sheikh Maqsood. [d3821855s1p0] Under Ba'athist rule and later during the Syrian Civil War, Kurds sought autonomy and in the context of the war established the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria. [d3821855s0p0] The Kurdistan Region promotes linguistic diversity by recognizing minority languages in administrative areas and establishing some schools using minority languages as the primary medium of instruction. [d3949386s23p0]
